The main takeaway from our work is that
levodopa is absorbed from the small intestine by the b0,+AT antiporter.

l-DOPA transport across intestinal enterocytes is mediated by the neutral amino acid transporter b0,+AT, which is not inhibited by the dopa-decarboylase or cathechol O-methyltransferase inhibitors that are routinely co-administered with levadopa.

levodopa transport across intestinal enterocytes is not mediated by large neutral amino acid transporters but rather by the b0,+AT transporter and that this transporter is a major determinant of levodopa absorption in the small intestine.
